name: Drug Discovery
tagline: Hit-to-lead optimization, ADMET profiling, and clinical candidate design.
seo_title: Drug Discovery — paper summaries, news & innovations | Chemisters
seo_description: Follow Chemisters Drug Discovery on LinkedIn and Facebook: paper summaries, news and innovations in target discovery, screening, AI-driven design, ADMET and clinical development.

definition.lead: Drug discovery is the long road from a disease target to a medicine: finding molecules that act on the target, then making them safe and effective enough for patients.
definition.body: It usually takes more than a decade and passes through target identification, hit finding, lead optimization, preclinical testing and clinical trials. Most candidates fail along the way, which is why better prediction, from AI to new screening methods, matters so much.

branches.name: Target identification
branches.summary: Finding the protein or pathway to act on.
branches.example: Human genetics linking a gene to a disease.

branches.name: Hit finding
branches.summary: Finding the first molecules that act on the target.

branches.name: Structure-based design
branches.summary: Using the target's 3D structure to design ligands.

branches.name: Virtual screening & AI
branches.summary: Predicting activity and properties in silico.
branches.example: Docking millions of molecules before testing any.

branches.name: ADMET profiling
branches.summary: Absorption, distribution, metabolism, excretion and toxicity.
branches.example: Predicting how fast the liver clears a drug.

branches.name: Clinical development

timeline.title: Penicillin
timeline.text: Alexander Fleming observes a mould killing bacteria.

timeline.title: Monoclonal antibodies
timeline.text: Georges Köhler and César Milstein produce identical antibodies from a single cell line.
timeline.why: The basis of today's antibody drugs.

timeline.title: Rational drug design
timeline.text: Nobel Prize in Medicine to James Black, Gertrude Elion and George Hitchings.
timeline.why: Drugs designed from an understanding of biochemistry.

timeline.title: Structure-based success
timeline.text: The first HIV protease inhibitor, saquinavir, is approved.
timeline.why: Designed with knowledge of the enzyme's structure.

timeline.title: Fragment-based discovery
timeline.text: Stephen Fesik's team links small fragments found by NMR into potent ligands.

timeline.title: The human genome
timeline.text: The first drafts of the human genome sequence are published.

timeline.title: mRNA vaccines
timeline.text: The first mRNA vaccines are authorized against COVID-19.
timeline.why: A new class of medicine in record time.

timeline.title: Predicted structures for all
timeline.text: AlphaFold's structure predictions are released in a public database.
timeline.why: Structural models for almost any target protein.

timeline.title: AI-designed candidates in trials
timeline.text: A candidate whose target and molecule were found with generative AI enters Phase 2 trials.
timeline.why: AI moved from papers into the clinic.
